title: Exceptional-adjoint admissibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of the valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$
[def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $S$-morphism. Choose a compactification
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements] $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline
X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, so $j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper. Use
finite-torsion constructibility
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], understood intrinsically as
boundedness and constructibility of the cohomology sheaves on the scheme
in question; no finite-field datum is required. The constructible sheaves
are those of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Write
$D(T,A)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived
category of sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient sheaf on the
small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. At the chosen
compactification set
$$
 F_c=Rf_{!,n}^c=Rp_{*,n}\,j_!:D(X,A)\longrightarrow D(Y,A),
$$
where $Rp_{*,n}$ is the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], and the extension by zero
[def-weil-extension-by-zero] is applied termwise to complexes; it induces
this derived functor by its exactness [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]
and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. This formula uses the
chosen compactification; no independence on all ambient inputs is
presupposed. Say that $f$ is
*exceptional-adjoint admissible at $A$* if:

1. the full cohomological-dimension condition
   [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension]
   $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c_{\mathrm{cd}})$ holds for some
   $c_{\mathrm{cd}}\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and there is a functor
   $Rf_n^{\times}:D(Y,A)\to D(X,A)$ that is a right
   adjoint to $F_c=Rf_{!,n}^c$ on $D(X,A)$ and $D(Y,A)$, meaning
   natural bijections
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,A)}(F_cK,L)\cong
   \operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,A)}(K,Rf_n^{\times}L)$ for all $K,L$.
   For every refinement its units, counits, and comparison maps agree.
   This last requirement is part of the datum: comparison isomorphisms
   between the compactification functors and between their right adjoints
   must identify the adjunction units and counits, be identities for
   identity refinements, and commute with composition. It is not inferred
   from an etale-origin comparison;
2. there are *signed* integers $c_f^-,c_f^+\in\mathbf Z$ such that, for every
   pair of integers $a\leq b$, with $D_c^{[a,b]}$ the constructible
   cohomological interval subcategory
   [def-weil-constructible-intervals],
   $$
    L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\Longrightarrow
    Rf_n^{\times}L\in D_c^{[a+c_f^-,b+c_f^+]}(X,A);
   $$
   if the shifted lower endpoint exceeds the upper endpoint, the interval
   denotes the zero subcategory (bounded constructible complexes with all
   cohomology sheaves zero). The constants record the cohomological bounds
   of the right adjoint. Their
   signs allow shifts in either direction; proving these bounds for a
   particular geometric morphism is a separate obligation.
3. for the finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]
   $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, one has
   $$
    L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)
   \Longrightarrow
    Rf_n^{\times}L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A).
   $$

At the remaining coefficient stages use the derived-complete integral
category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its raw rationalization
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] (without idempotent completion), and the
common-stage algebraically closed coefficient category
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Admissibility at these stages is
a condition on the finite systems, as follows; it does not take a freely
specified diagram of higher coefficient categories as input.

For each finite coefficient ring map $\phi:A\to B$, let $T_{\phi,Z}$ be
actual derived extension of scalars on $D(Z,A)$, the left adjoint of the
exact restriction of scalars $U_{\phi,Z}$. Use the compact-support functor
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and its canonical restriction
comparison $U_{\phi,X}F_A\cong F_B U_{\phi,Y}$
[lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Transposing this comparison
under the coefficient adjunctions gives
$\alpha_\phi:T_{\phi,Y}F_A\to F_BT_{\phi,X}$.
When the ambient adjoints are chosen, $F_A$ preserves coproducts, so this
canonical tensor comparison is invertible. The right coefficient map is
EXACTLY the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of
$\alpha_\phi^{-1}$ under those same chosen ambient adjunctions:
$$\beta_\phi:T_{\phi,X}G_A\longrightarrow G_BT_{\phi,Y}.$$
Changing from the fixed-scalar presentation to the intrinsic constant-ring
presentation transports the adjunctions and comparisons together; it does
not permit a new coefficient comparison.

At $\mathcal O_E$ choose the ambient adjunction/refinement datum at every
$A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, with the three displayed conditions and a single set
of bounds independent of $n$. Require $\beta_\phi$ to be an isomorphism
for EVERY quotient $\phi:A_{E,n}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,m}$,
$1\leq m\leq n$, including $m=n$. For every finite coefficient extension
$\iota:E\hookrightarrow L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose the corresponding
family at $A_{L,n}$ with bounds independent of $n$ and the same quotient
compatibilities, and require $\beta_\phi$ to be an isomorphism for every
$\phi:A_{E,n}\to A_{L,n}$ induced by the valuation-ring inclusion,
including identity embeddings. These are derived tensor maps, not
underived tensor maps for nonflat quotients. The scalar ring maps are the
finite projections of completed integral scalar extension
[def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. At $E$, impose this same finite-system
criterion before raw rationalization.

At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ choose a fixed algebraic closure and one
ambient family at EVERY finite intermediate field
[def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] and EVERY positive exponent.
Require one common set of bounds independent of the field and exponent,
all the quotient compatibilities just specified, and all the scalar
compatibilities induced by inclusions of finite intermediate fields,
including identities. The finite intermediate fields are nonempty (the
base field is one of them). This is the finite-system criterion before
the common-stage construction. It contains no optional reduction or
scalar-extension index set. The corresponding normalized integral systems,
raw rationalizations and common-stage objects have their recorded meanings;
this criterion does not assert existence of a new unconditional ambient
exceptional adjoint at any stage. All these conditions remain proof
obligations, not consequences of being separated and finite type.

*Warning.* Clause (1) is not satisfied in general: its
$\operatorname{FullCD}$ condition fails for the structure morphism of an
elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$, $r\neq p$,
and for that morphism $Rf_!=Rf_*$ has no right adjoint on the ambient derived
category, nor on $D^+$ (rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors
chapter). Hence the structure morphism of a smooth proper variety may *not*
be presupposed exceptional-adjoint admissible in this sense, and no statement
on the proof chain of this blueprint assumes it. What the blueprint uses is
the constructible exceptional adjoint of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image,
defined without clause (1) from the etale adjoint; for it the analogues of
(1)–(3) on $D^b_c$ and $D^b_{ctf}$ are theorems for every separated
finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes (thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class
for the adjunction, thm-sf-preservation-class for the two preservation
clauses with the constants $c_f^-=-2D$, $c_f^+=2\dim Y+1$). The present
definition is retained only to name the stronger, optional, ambient notion.

split_report.summary: Definition split into existing ingredients only, with all six seeded definition dependencies retained. Made the finite coefficient ring, ordinary unbounded pro-etale derived categories, chosen-compactification functor Rp_* j_!, and the exactness required to induce j_! on derived categories explicit. Expanded adjunction and refinement compatibility as conditional data, with no ambient compactification-independence assertion. Named the integral, rational and common-stage coefficient categories, reductions, scalar extensions and adjunction mates. Clarified the empty shifted-interval convention without imposing sign restrictions or weakening any condition. The related slopmaster2 structure omits refinement and coefficient compatibility and is not an attachment. No new nodes and no proof steps for this definition.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the definition at blueprint order 1474, clauses (1), (2), (3) and its coefficient-stage paragraph, in the ambient-operation route sk-def-sf-operations(iv)-(v). Does not replace the optional ambient adjoint by the unconditional constructible adjoint of (vi); preserves the source warning as a scope remark. Imported blueprint node has from=null; whole-blueprint searches found no equal definition.

lean.statement: def IsExceptionalAdjointAdmissibleAtFiniteStage (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (S X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] (_hS : ∀ s : S, IsUnit (l : S.presheaf.stalk s)) [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ S)] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ S)] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ S)] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ S)] (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver S] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (c : Compactification f) : Prop

statement_change.what: The stage-1 expansion identified the finite-system coefficient criterion with unspecified integral-to-finite and higher-category squares. Neither the source paragraph nor the unit defines such arbitrary square data. The original source states the criterion at every finite stage, and unit sk-def-sf-operations (vi) explicitly uses the quotient maps A_(E,n) to A_(E,m) before normalization, rationalization and common stages. This correction makes the quantifiers and canonical mates explicit, including identity arrows and the nonempty common-stage field index, instead of adding arbitrary higher comparison data. No finite-stage clause or unit statement changes.
